subject: Identity connector & access patterns for Private Control Plane - design review

Subject: Identity connector & access patterns for Private Control Plane - design review

Hi Neha / team,

Thanks for agreeing to look at our Private Control Plane integration. Attached are the current IdP assertion mapping and our network diagram (acme-idp-assertion-mapping.pdf, network-diagram-v2.png). High level asks from Acme infra: 

- We need SSO for engineers and SAML assertions that map to Redwood roles (admin, infra, app-runner).
- Automated user provisioning and deprovisioning (SCIM) with 15 min sync target.
- A model for service accounts used by CI/CD that avoids long-lived keys.
- Clear network patterns: SCIM traffic should traverse our Transit Gateway -> PrivateLink to Redwood control plane.
- Audit trail/retention: 7 years preferred for compliance.

Can you confirm whether Redwood supports: group-to-role mapping, a SCIM push vs pull model, and whether mutual TLS or IP allowlist is required? Also propose an approach for the CI/CD service accounts (OIDC, short-lived tokens?).

We'd like a short design review next week (30 min). Proposed times: Tue/Wed morning PT.

Thanks,
Jules
Infrastructure Lead, Acme Corporation

--

Subject: Re: Identity connector & access patterns for Private Control Plane - design review

Hi Jules — thanks for the materials, they were helpful. Quick answers up front, then a proposed agenda for the design call: 

Short answers:
- Group-to-role mapping: supported. We use an internal "role projection" layer that consumes SAML attributes + SCIM group membership to produce ephemeral RBAC tokens.
- SCIM model: we support both push and pull. For private deployments we generally recommend a customer-initiated connector (SCIM relay) inside the customer VPC that forwards provisioning traffic over PrivateLink. This avoids exposing SCIM endpoints publicly and lets the customer manage egress.
- Mutual TLS: recommended for SCIM push. We also support token-backed SCIM if mTLS is not feasible.
- Service accounts: recommend OIDC-based short-lived tokens for CI/CD; we can map federated identities to scoped service roles in the control plane.
- Audit retention: we can configure per-tenant retention up to 7 years; we will need SLAs for storage costs.

Proposed 30-min agenda:
1) Quick review of assertion mapping (5m)
2) Role projection and SCIM mapping (10m)
3) Connectivity patterns (PrivateLink, peering, relay) and mTLS (10m)
4) Actions & next steps (5m)

I've attached a starter "redwood-role-mapping.json" with examples for how group -> role projection works in our system.

Can you confirm Wed 09:30 PT?

—Neha
Neha Kapoor

Looping in a few implementation constraints from the runtime/infra perspective: 

- SCIM semantics: ensure idempotency. Our SCIM implementation expects patch/update semantics and will reconcile on receipt; large group deltas can be expensive. Recommend limiting group->role mappings to ~50 rules per tenant or pre-batching large syncs.
- Attribute names: some IdPs expose 'memberOf', others 'groups'. We'll use a configurable attribute key (default: 'groups'). The mapping supports regex-based matching for nested groups.
- Connectivity: for Private Control Plane the control plane listener sits behind an internal ALB exposed via PrivateLink. SCIM push traffic must originate from within the customer's VPC or via a mutually authenticated TLS tunnel.
- Mutual TLS: we will require client certs for SCIM push in high-security deployments; otherwise token-based SCIM with an IP allowlist is the fallback.
- Service accounts: avoid long-lived API keys. We issue short-lived JWTs signed by Redwood KMS; tokens are <1h TTL by default. For CI federation use-case we recommend OIDC trust between your IdP and Redwood, and a mapping to a scoped service role.

I'll bring a sample replay that shows SCIM retry backoff and patch semantics to the call.

-Markus
Principal Engineer, Runtime

Subject: Re: Identity connector & access patterns for Private Control Plane - design review

Jules — ops notes from our side ahead of the call: 

1) SCIM relay option: we propose shipping a small container (docker image) you can run in your VPC. It authenticates to your IdP and forwards SCIM updates to Redwood over PrivateLink. Benefits: 1) no public SCIM endpoints; 2) connection originates from your VPC so firewall rules are straightforward; 3) relay can buffer during network blips.

2) Push vs pull tradeoffs: push is lower-latency for deprovisioning; pull reduces reliance on customer-run processes. Given your 15-min SLA for sync, relay + push looks ideal.

3) Network: we'll need the following open on your side: outbound TLS to our PrivateLink endpoint (TCP 443), and for mutual TLS mode the relay will present a client cert we issue. If PrivateLink is not an option, a site-to-site VPN peer is acceptable.

4) Audit/logging: relay will forward an audit bundle to Redwood; we recommend enabling Hash-based Message Authentication (HMAC) on those bundles for integrity. We'll include a per-event UUID so you can reconcile.

Next steps we suggest:
- Test with a canary tenant and a restricted group set (5 users, 2 groups).
- Run a scripted deprovision test to validate TTL and audit events.

I'll capture these action items on the call and follow up with a short runbook for your SREs.

Thanks,
Mateo
